findings.title: SendGrid `@sendgrid/client` API key is never initialized in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`
findings.body: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` at line 19, but never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` on the imported `@sendgrid/client` instance (unlike `emailReminderManager.ts` which sets both at lines 25-26). In serverless / isolated route environments where `emailReminderManager.ts` has not been imported in the same process, `client.request(...)` at lines 57 and 188 will fail with an unauthorized error from SendGrid, preventing both the cancellation of scheduled emails and the creation of batch IDs for newly scheduled emails.

findings.title: Rescheduling a booking immediately cancels SendGrid batch IDs instead of deferring to the cron job
findings.body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, when cancelling workflow reminders of the original rescheduled booking, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete = true`. Inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, `immediateDelete = true` bypasses setting `cancelled: true` in the database and immediately calls `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` on SendGrid (and also leaves the `WorkflowReminder` row in the database without deleting it or marking it cancelled). This directly defeats the purpose of the PR for rescheduled bookings—it will still hit SendGrid's 100 pending `scheduled_sends` limit when bookings are rescheduled more than 1 hour in advance—and leaves stale `WorkflowReminder` records attached to the rescheduled booking.

findings.title: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` with `immediateDelete = true` does not delete the `WorkflowReminder` database record
findings.body: When `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called with `immediateDelete = true` (e.g., when a workflow or step is deleted, or during booking reschedule), it sends the cancel request to SendGrid and returns early at line 222 without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row from `prisma.workflowReminder`. For booking reschedules (`handleNewBooking.ts`), the row is not cascade-deleted because the original booking row is kept with `status: CANCELLED`, leaving orphaned `WorkflowReminder` rows in the database until their `scheduledDate` passes.

findings.title: Cancelling a paid booking returns early before cancelling workflow reminders or scheduled jobs
findings.body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, if `bookingToDelete.paid` is true (lines 363-465), the handler refunds the payment, marks the booking as `REJECTED`, and returns at line 464. Because the loop that cancels `workflowReminders` (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`) is at lines 485-493 after this early return, workflow reminders for cancelled paid bookings are never cancelled and will still be sent to the attendee and host.

findings.title: Unawaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls before deleting workflow or step
findings.body: In `workflowsRouter.delete` (lines 212-225) and `workflowsRouter.update` when a step is deleted (lines 519-531), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are invoked inside `.forEach(...)` without `await`, immediately followed by `await ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany(...)` or `await ctx.prisma.workflowStep.delete(...)`. Because `WorkflowReminder` has `onDelete: Cascade` on `workflowStepId`, the cascade delete races with the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` calls inside `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (when `referenceId` is null), causing `Record to delete does not exist` Prisma errors, and in serverless environments the unawaited SendGrid/Twilio network requests may be terminated after the mutation response returns.
